claim: The evolutionary expansion of extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules has been crucial for the establishment of cell adhesion and the transition from unicellular to multicellular life.
source: The evolutionary expansion of extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules has been crucial for the establishment of cell adhesion and the transition from unicellular to multicellular life.
evidence: This is a statement about the evolutionary role of ECM molecules, drawing from established scientific consensus about the evolution of multicellularity.

claim: Members of the early diverging metazoan phylum Cnidaria offer an exceptionally rich perspective into the metazoan core adhesome and its original function in developmental and morphogenetic processes.
source: Members of the early diverging metazoan phylum Cnidaria offer an exceptionally rich perspective into the metazoan core adhesome and its original function in developmental and morphogenetic processes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the study's findings and the phylogenetic position of cnidarians as early-diverging metazoans.

claim: The study presents the ensemble of ECM proteins and associated factors for the starlet sea anemone Nematostella vectensis based on in silico prediction and quantitative proteomic analysis of decellularized mesoglea from different life stages.
source: Here, we present the ensemble of ECM proteins and associated factors for the starlet sea anemone Nematostella vectensis based on in silico prediction and quantitative proteomic analysis of decellularized mesoglea from different life stages.
evidence: This describes the methodology and scope of the study, which is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Gastrodermal cells are the primary producers of Nematostella's complex ECM.
source: The integration of the matrisome with single-cell transcriptome atlases shows that gastrodermal cells are the primary producers of Nematostella's complex ECM, confirming the homology of the cnidarian inner cell layer with bilaterian mesoderm.
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell transcriptome data integrated with the matrisome analysis.

claim: The cnidarian inner cell layer is homologous to bilaterian mesoderm.
source: The integration of the matrisome with single-cell transcriptome atlases shows that gastrodermal cells are the primary producers of Nematostella's complex ECM, confirming the homology of the cnidarian inner cell layer with bilaterian mesoderm.
evidence: This claim is supported by the finding that gastrodermal cells produce ECM, which is consistent with the role of mesoderm in bilaterians.

claim: The transition from larva to polyp is marked by an upregulation of metalloproteases and basement membrane components.
source: The transition from larva to polyp is marked by an upregulation of metalloproteases and basement membrane components including all members of an unusually diversified SVEP1/Polydom family, suggesting massive epithelial remodeling.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative proteomic data comparing different life stages.

claim: All members of an unusually diversified SVEP1/Polydom family are upregulated during the transition from larva to polyp.
source: The transition from larva to polyp is marked by an upregulation of metalloproteases and basement membrane components including all members of an unusually diversified SVEP1/Polydom family, suggesting massive epithelial remodeling.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative proteomic data showing upregulation of all Polydom family members.

claim: The upregulation of metalloproteases and basement membrane components during larva-to-polyp transition suggests massive epithelial remodeling.
source: The transition from larva to polyp is marked by an upregulation of metalloproteases and basement membrane components including all members of an unusually diversified SVEP1/Polydom family, suggesting massive epithelial remodeling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the proteomic data based on the known functions of metalloproteases and basement membrane components.

claim: The enrichment of Wnt/PCP pathway factors during larva-to-polyp transition indicates directed cell rearrangements as a key contributor to the polyp's morphogenesis.
source: The enrichment of Wnt/PCP pathway factors during this process further indicates directed cell rearrangements as a key contributor to the polyp's morphogenesis.
evidence: This is based on proteomic data showing enrichment of Wnt/PCP factors and knowledge of their role in cell rearrangements.

claim: Mesoglea maturation in adult polyps involves wound response proteins.
source: Mesoglea maturation in adult polyps involves wound response proteins indicating shared molecular patterns in growth and regeneration.
evidence: This is supported by proteomic data showing the presence of wound response proteins in adult polyps.

claim: The presence of wound response proteins in adult polyp mesoglea indicates shared molecular patterns in growth and regeneration.
source: Mesoglea maturation in adult polyps involves wound response proteins indicating shared molecular patterns in growth and regeneration.
evidence: This is an inference based on the presence of wound response proteins and their known functions.

claim: Some ECM components, such as integrins and cadherin receptors, can be traced back to unicellular organisms.
source: While some ECM components, such as integrins and cadherin receptors, can be traced back to unicellular organisms (Nichols et al., 2012; Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2010), early diverging cnidarians (hydroids, jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones) are believed to possess one of the most complete adhesomes among non-bilaterian clades (Ozbek et al., 2010; Tucker and Adams, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Early diverging cnidarians are believed to possess one of the most complete adhesomes among non-bilaterian clades.
source: While some ECM components, such as integrins and cadherin receptors, can be traced back to unicellular organisms (Nichols et al., 2012; Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2010), early diverging cnidarians (hydroids, jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones) are believed to possess one of the most complete adhesomes among non-bilaterian clades (Ozbek et al., 2010; Tucker and Adams, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cnidarians are the sister group to bilaterians.
source: Cnidarians, the sister group to bilaterians, are characterized by a simple body plan with a central body cavity and a mouth opening surrounded by tentacles.
evidence: This is a statement based on established phylogenetic knowledge.

claim: Cnidarians are diploblastic organisms, consisting of an outer epithelium and an inner gastrodermis separated by a complex ECM called mesoglea.
source: They are diploblastic organisms, consisting of an outer epithelium and an inner gastrodermis separated by a complex ECM called mesoglea (Bergheim and Özbek, 2019; Sarras, 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about cnidarian anatomy supported by citations.

claim: The mesoglea in Hydra forms a flexible, tri-laminar structure composed of a central, amorphous interstitial matrix (IM) interspersed with collagenous fibrils, sandwiched between two thin layers of basement membrane (BM).
source: The mesoglea, which is best studied in the freshwater polyp Hydra, forms a flexible, tri-laminar structure. It is composed of a central, amorphous interstitial matrix (IM) interspersed with collagenous fibrils, sandwiched between two thin layers of basement membrane (BM) (Aufschnaiter et al., 2011; Bergheim and Özbek, 2019; Sarras et al., 1991; Shimizu et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on Hydra mesoglea structure.

claim: The mesoglea in Hydra can be separated intact from the epithelial cell sheets by a freeze-thaw technique.
source: Studies in Hydra have shown that the mesoglea can be separated intact from the epithelial cell sheets by a freeze-thaw technique (Day and Lenhoff, 1981; Veschgini et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The proteome of decellularized Hydra mesoglea contains 37 unique protein sequences.
source: Previously, we analyzed the proteome of decellularized Hydra mesoglea and identified 37 unique protein sequences (Lommel et al., 2018), including most of the described core matrisome components (Sarras, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Hydras have lost the free-swimming medusa form.
source: Among medusozoans (jellyfish and hydroids), hydras stand out for having lost the free-swimming medusa form.
evidence: This is a statement about hydra biology based on established knowledge.

claim: Hydras lack a planula larva stage from which anthozoans typically produce sessile polyps.
source: They also lack a planula larva stage from which anthozoans (corals and sea anemones) typically produce sessile polyps.
evidence: This is a statement about hydra and anthozoan life cycles based on established knowledge.

claim: The study identified 1812 potential ECM proteins in Nematostella vectensis.
source: Building on this knowledge and a de novo annotation of all predicted Nematostella protein models using InterProScan (Jones et al., 2014), we identified 1812 potential ECM proteins (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the in silico prediction methodology described and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The study narrowed down the number of high-confidence ECM genes in Nematostella to 829.
source: After manually excluding duplicates and sequencing artifacts, we narrowed down the number of high-confidence ECM genes defined by the possession of a bona fide ECM domain (Hynes and Naba, 2012) to 829 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the manual curation process described and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mass spectrometry analysis identified 287 ECM components in the isolated Nematostella mesogleas, of which 210 belonged to the matrisome.
source: To address this, we used our curated in silico list of 829 candidate ECM genes as a filter and identified 287 ECM components in the isolated Nematostella mesogleas, of which 210 belonged to the matrisome (Figure 1B, Supplementary files 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by the mass spectrometry data and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The number of matrisomal proteins detected in Nematostella (210) exceeds the previously reported 37 matrisomal proteins in Hydra.
source: This number exceeds the previously reported 37 matrisomal proteins in Hydra (Lommel et al., 2018), suggesting a greater compositional diversity in Nematostella.
evidence: This is a comparison of the current study's findings with a previous study on Hydra.

claim: The Nematostella mesoglea has higher complexity than the Hydra mesoglea, particularly in the lower molecular weight fraction.
source: A comparison of mesoglea samples of both species resolved by protein gel electrophoresis confirmed the higher complexity of the Nematostella mesoglea, particularly in the lower molecular weight fraction (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by protein gel electrophoresis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Nematostella matrisome comprises 551 proteins, representing approximately 3% of its proteome.
source: In summary, the Nematostella matrisome comprises 551 proteins, representing approximately 3% of its proteome (Artamonova and Mushegian, 2013) and roughly half the size of the human matrisome with 1056 proteins (Naba et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on the study's findings and comparison with the total proteome size.

claim: The Nematostella matrisome is roughly half the size of the human matrisome with 1056 proteins.
source: In summary, the Nematostella matrisome comprises 551 proteins, representing approximately 3% of its proteome (Artamonova and Mushegian, 2013) and roughly half the size of the human matrisome with 1056 proteins (Naba et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison with the human matrisome size from a cited study.

claim: The Nematostella core matrisome is comparable to that of bilaterians.
source: While the Nematostella core matrisome is comparable to that of bilaterians, vertebrate species exhibit a dramatic expansion in ECM-associated factors (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the comparison shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Vertebrate species exhibit a dramatic expansion in ECM-associated factors compared to Nematostella.
source: While the Nematostella core matrisome is comparable to that of bilaterians, vertebrate species exhibit a dramatic expansion in ECM-associated factors (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the comparison shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The Nematostella core matrisome includes 241 proteins, including collagens, proteoglycans, and ECM glycoproteins.
source: Within this core matrisome, we identified 241 proteins, including collagens, proteoglycans, and ECM glycoproteins (e.g. laminins; Fahey and Degnan, 2012) and thrombospondins (Shoemark et al., 2019; Tucker et al., 2013; Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by the classification of proteins shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The study identified a set of 310 'matrisome-associated' factors in Nematostella.
source: Additionally, we identified a set of 310 'matrisome-associated' factors.
evidence: This is based on the classification of proteins in the study.

claim: The laminin antibody stains the bilaminar structure of the basement membrane at the base of the epithelial cell layers.
source: In cross-sections, the laminin antibody stained the thin double layer of the basement membrane (BM) lining the two epithelia, while the PanCol antibody detected the intervening fibrous layer of the interstitial matrix (IM; Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The pan-Collagen antibody detects the central interstitial matrix.
source: In cross-sections, the laminin antibody stained the thin double layer of the basement membrane (BM) lining the two epithelia, while the PanCol antibody detected the intervening fibrous layer of the interstitial matrix (IM; Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The mesoglea has a mean thickness of approximately 0.5 µm in larvae and 1.5 µm in primary polyps.
source: Ultrastructural examination of the mesoglea revealed a mean thickness of approximately 0.5 µm in larvae and 1.5 µm in primary polyps (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B, G–H, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The basement membrane lining the epithelia of larvae is very delicate, measuring only 70 nm.
source: The BM lining the epithelia of larvae was very delicate, measuring only 70 nm, and the IM appeared as a loose array of thin fibrils (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Primary polyps possess a distinct basement membrane with a thickness of approximately 130 nm.
source: Primary polyps possessed a distinct BM, with a thickness of approximately 130 nm, appearing as a dense meshwork of fibrils (Figure 1—figure supplement 3H, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3H.

claim: Core matrisome genes show above average expression scores in the mature gastrodermis and developing cnidocytes.
source: We calculated an average expression score for each of the ECM gene sets (core and associated matrisome, adhesome/other) and found above average scores for the core matrisome associated with the mature gastrodermis and developing cnidocytes, and to a lesser extent also for the other two categories (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: There is an absence of any differentially expressed core matrisome factors within the ectodermal tissues.
source: Of note is the absence of any differentially expressed core matrisome factors within the ectodermal tissues, and contrastingly, a large set that are specific to either the mesoendodermal inner cell layer (gastrodermis) or cnidocytes (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A large set of core matrisome genes are specific to either the mesoendodermal inner cell layer (gastrodermis) or cnidocytes.
source: Of note is the absence of any differentially expressed core matrisome factors within the ectodermal tissues, and contrastingly, a large set that are specific to either the mesoendodermal inner cell layer (gastrodermis) or cnidocytes (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Core components of the mesoglea (collagens, laminins) are produced from the inner cell layer.
source: Altogether, these expression profiles suggest that core components of the mesoglea (collagens, laminins) are produced from the inner cell layer, and that a large set of ECM glycoproteins and all of the minicollagens David et al., 2008; Zenkert et al., 2011 have been recruited into the formation of the cnidarian synapomorphy, the cnidocytes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the single-cell RNA expression data.

claim: A large set of ECM glycoproteins and all of the minicollagens have been recruited into the formation of cnidocytes.
source: Altogether, these expression profiles suggest that core components of the mesoglea (collagens, laminins) are produced from the inner cell layer, and that a large set of ECM glycoproteins and all of the minicollagens David et al., 2008; Zenkert et al., 2011 have been recruited into the formation of the cnidarian synapomorphy, the cnidocytes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the single-cell RNA expression data and citations.

claim: The study identified 12 bilaterian-type collagens in Nematostella.
source: Our analysis revealed 12 bilaterian-type collagens (Figure 2C) with conserved C-terminal non-collagenous trimerization domains (NC1) and extended triple helical stretches of ~1000 residues, including two sequences for type IV collagen (NvCol4a/b) together with a peroxidasin homolog (NV2.13306), indicating the presence of sulfilimine cross-links that stabilize the Nematostella BM (Fidler et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by the domain analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Nematostella has two sequences for type IV collagen (NvCol4a/b) together with a peroxidasin homolog, indicating the presence of sulfilimine cross-links that stabilize the Nematostella basement membrane.
source: Our analysis revealed 12 bilaterian-type collagens (Figure 2C) with conserved C-terminal non-collagenous trimerization domains (NC1) and extended triple helical stretches of ~1000 residues, including two sequences for type IV collagen (NvCol4a/b) together with a peroxidasin homolog (NV2.13306), indicating the presence of sulfilimine cross-links that stabilize the Nematostella BM (Fidler et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on the identification of collagen IV and peroxidasin, with inference about sulfilimine cross-links supported by a citation.

claim: Hydra lacks sulfilimine cross-links in its basement membrane.
source: In Hydra, which lacks this specific post-translational modification, six collagen genes have been identified through cDNA cloning and proteomic analysis (Deutzmann et al., 2000; Fowler et al., 2000; Lommel et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about Hydra, supported by citations.

claim: Six collagen genes have been identified in Hydra through cDNA cloning and proteomic analysis.
source: In Hydra, which lacks this specific post-translational modification, six collagen genes have been identified through cDNA cloning and proteomic analysis (Deutzmann et al., 2000; Fowler et al., 2000; Lommel et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The study identified three isoforms of NvCol1 in Nematostella.
source: We have classified the collagens according to the Hydra nomenclature (Zhang et al., 2007) and identified three isoforms of NvCol1, each comprising an isolated minor triple helical domain at the N-terminus (Figure 2C, upper panel).
evidence: This is supported by the domain analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The study detected four NvCol2 paralogs in Nematostella, which contain an additional whey acidic protein 4 disulfide core (WAP) domain at the N-terminus.
source: In addition, we detected four NvCol2 paralogs, which contain an additional whey acidic protein 4 disulfide core (WAP) domain at the N-terminus.
evidence: This is supported by the domain analysis.

claim: Most of the Nematostella collagens show a broad expression in diverse gastrodermal cell populations throughout all life stages.
source: Most of the Nematostella collagens show a broad expression in diverse gastrodermal cell populations throughout all life stages (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: NvCol2c is predominantly expressed in neuronal cells of larvae, indicating a specialized function in neurogenesis.
source: NvCol2c is an exception, as it is predominantly expressed in neuronal cells of larvae, indicating a specialized function in neurogenesis.
evidence: This is based on single-cell RNA expression data and inference about its function.

claim: NvCol4a is additionally expressed during embryogenesis, emphasizing the pivotal role of the basement membrane in organizing the epithelial tissue architecture during early development.
source: Unlike the IM collagens, NvCol4a is additionally expressed during embryogenesis, emphasizing the pivotal role of the BM in organizing the epithelial tissue architecture during early development.
evidence: This is based on expression data and inference about the role of basement membrane.

claim: The study identified four spongin-like proteins in Nematostella, which are short-chain collagens with derived NC1 domains.
source: In addition to these bilaterian-type collagens, we have identified four spongin-like proteins, which are short-chain collagens with derived NC1 domains (Figure 2C, middle panel).
evidence: This is supported by the domain analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Spongin-like proteins have been described as truncated variants of collagen IV with a wide distribution in several invertebrate phyla.
source: These molecules have been described as truncated variants of collagen IV with a wide distribution in several invertebrate phyla (Aouacheria et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The large set of minicollagens is strictly aligned with the cnidocyte lineage.
source: In contrast, the large set of minicollagens (Figure 2C, lower panel) is strictly aligned with the cnidocyte lineage as detailed below.
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data.

claim: The study filtered the dataset of 829 curated ECM protein-coding sequences for genes expressed within cnidocytes and found 298 genes detectable above average in at least 5% of any cnidocyte transcriptomic state.
source: We filtered the dataset of the 829 curated ECM protein-coding sequences for genes expressed within cnidocytes and found 298 genes that are detectable above average in at least 5% of any cnidocyte transcriptomic state (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: 101 cnidocyte-expressed genes are absent from non-cnidocyte states ('exclusive').
source: We further separated this list of genes into those that are absent from non-cnidocyte states (101 genes: 'exclusive') or are also detected within more than 50% of the non-cnidocyte transcriptomic states (41 genes: 'ubiquitous'; Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 41 cnidocyte-expressed genes are also detected within more than 50% of the non-cnidocyte transcriptomic states ('ubiquitous').
source: We further separated this list of genes into those that are absent from non-cnidocyte states (101 genes: 'exclusive') or are also detected within more than 50% of the non-cnidocyte transcriptomic states (41 genes: 'ubiquitous'; Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 79 cnidocyte-specific genes are restricted to the capsule-building specification phase ('specification').
source: Of the cnidocyte-specific genes, we examined the proportion of genes specific to either the capsule-building specification profiles (79: 'specification') or the maturation phase of cnidogenesis (24: 'maturation').
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data.

claim: 24 cnidocyte-specific genes are associated with the maturation phase of cnidogenesis ('maturation').
source: Of the cnidocyte-specific genes, we examined the proportion of genes specific to either the capsule-building specification profiles (79: 'specification') or the maturation phase of cnidogenesis (24: 'maturation').
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data.

claim: The study identified all five previously described Nematostella minicollagen sequences (NvCol-1,–3, −4,–5, –6) along with four additional proteins with incomplete minicollagen sequence features, termed 'minicollagen-like'.
source: We identified all five previously described Nematostella minicollagen sequences (Steger et al., 2022; Zenkert et al., 2011) (NvCol-1,–3, −4,–5, –6) along with four additional proteins with incomplete minicollagen sequence features, which we termed 'minicollagen-like' (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by the domain analysis shown in Figure 2C and citations.

claim: The study identified a protein (NvNCol-7) that combines features of both minicollagens and extended ECM-type collagens, suggesting a possible evolutionary origin of minicollagens from this gene family.
source: Intriguingly, we also identified a protein that combines features of both minicollagens and extended ECM-type collagens, suggesting a possible evolutionary origin of minicollagens from this gene family. This protein, NvNCol-7, contains a minicollagen pro-peptide sequence, proline-rich regions, and canonical N- and C-terminal CRDs (Tursch et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on the domain analysis of NvNCol-7 and inference about evolutionary origin.

claim: Nematostella minicollagens exhibit differential expression across different cnidocyte subtypes, nematocytes, and spirocytes.
source: Interestingly, Nematostella minicollagens exhibit differential expression across different cnidocyte subtypes, nematocytes, and spirocytes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A significant fraction (32%) of matrisomal genes (176 of 551) are expressed within the cnidocyte lineage.
source: In summary, a significant fraction (32%) of matrisomal genes (176 of 551, Supplementary file 6) are expressed within the cnidocyte lineage.
evidence: This is based on the analysis of single-cell RNA expression data.

claim: The proportion of cnidarian-specific factors in the cnidocyte-expressed matrisome subset (48%) is increased compared to the full matrisome (42%).
source: The proportion of cnidarian-specific factors in this subset is increased (85 of 176, 48%) as compared to the full matrisome (234 of 551, 42%, Supplementary file 1), supporting the notion that the cnidocyte proteome represents a specialized ECM adapted to the unique assembly process and biophysical requirements of the cnidarian stinging organelle (Balasubramanian et al., 2012; Ozbek, 2011).
evidence: This is based on the analysis of the matrisome composition and supported by citations.

claim: The cnidocyte proteome represents a specialized ECM adapted to the unique assembly process and biophysical requirements of the cnidarian stinging organelle.
source: The proportion of cnidarian-specific factors in this subset is increased (85 of 176, 48%) as compared to the full matrisome (234 of 551, 42%, Supplementary file 1), supporting the notion that the cnidocyte proteome represents a specialized ECM adapted to the unique assembly process and biophysical requirements of the cnidarian stinging organelle (Balasubramanian et al., 2012; Ozbek, 2011).
evidence: This is an inference based on the data and supported by citations.

claim: Larva-polyp morphogenesis in Nematostella involves significant changes in body shape including the elongation of the body axis and the development of oral tentacles and internal mesenteries.
source: Larva-polyp morphogenesis in Nematostella involves significant changes in body shape including the elongation of the body axis and the development of oral tentacles and internal mesenteries (Stokkermans et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement about Nematostella development supported by a citation.

claim: 38% (210 of 551) of the matrisomal factors were detected by mass spectrometry analysis.
source: As shown above, 38% (210 of 551) of the matrisomal factors were detected by our mass spectrometry analysis (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is based on the mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 94 proteins were differentially upregulated in primary polyps compared to larvae.
source: 94 proteins were differentially upregulated in primary polyps while only four, including vitellogenin and its receptor that are crucial for lipid transport from the ECM into the oocyte (Lebouvier et al., 2022), were differentially abundant in larvae.
evidence: This is based on quantitative proteomic data.

claim: Only four proteins, including vitellogenin and its receptor, were differentially abundant in larvae compared to primary polyps.
source: 94 proteins were differentially upregulated in primary polyps while only four, including vitellogenin and its receptor that are crucial for lipid transport from the ECM into the oocyte (Lebouvier et al., 2022), were differentially abundant in larvae.
evidence: This is based on quantitative proteomic data and a citation about vitellogenin function.

claim: Vitellogenin and its receptor are crucial for lipid transport from the ECM into the oocyte.
source: 94 proteins were differentially upregulated in primary polyps while only four, including vitellogenin and its receptor that are crucial for lipid transport from the ECM into the oocyte (Lebouvier et al., 2022), were differentially abundant in larvae.
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The proteins enriched in primary polyps compared to larvae include factors involved in basement membrane establishment and remodeling, and components of the Wnt/PCP signaling pathway.
source: The proteins enriched in primary polyps as compared to larvae include, in addition to various factors involved in general cell adhesion (e.g. cadherin-1, coadhesin-like proteins), two major functional groups (Figure 4C, Supplementary file 7): (1) factors involved in BM establishment and remodeling and (2) components of the Wnt/PCP signaling pathway.
evidence: This is based on quantitative proteomic data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The enrichment of basement membrane and Wnt/PCP factors is indicative of massive epithelial rearrangement, rather than cell proliferation, as a driver of larva-to-polyp transition.
source: Both groups are indicative of a massive epithelial rearrangement, rather than cell proliferation, as a driver of larva-to-polyp transition (Stokkermans et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an inference based on the proteomic data and supported by a citation.

claim: The study identified an unusually expanded Polydom protein family in Nematostella.
source: Notably, in addition to laminins, the BM proteoglycan perlecan and numerous astacin, ADAMTS, and MMP family metalloproteases (see Figure 4—figure supplement 2 for an overview), the first group contained all members of an unusually expanded Polydom protein family (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is based on the identification and domain analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Polydom/SVEP1 is a secreted multidomain ECM protein initially discovered in a murine bone-marrow stromal cell line.
source: Polydom/SVEP1 is a secreted multidomain ECM protein initially discovered in a murine bone-marrow stromal cell line (Gilgès et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Polydom has recently been shown to be a ligand for the orphan receptor Tie1 and induce lymphatic vessel remodeling via PI3K/Akt signaling.
source: Polydom has recently been shown to be a ligand for the orphan receptor Tie1 and induce lymphatic vessel remodeling via PI3K/Akt signaling (Sato-Nishiuchi et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Earlier studies have shown basement membrane deposition of Polydom and a role in epithelial cell-cell adhesion via integrin binding.
source: Earlier studies have shown basement membrane deposition of Polydom and a role in epithelial cell-cell adhesion via integrin binding (Samuelov et al., 2017; Sato-Nishiuchi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: The Hydractinia Polydom homolog has been characterized as a factor specific to i-cells and to be potentially involved in innate immunity.
source: The Hydractinia homolog has been characterized as a factor specific to i-cells and to be potentially involved in innate immunity (Schwarz et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The study identified a Nematostella Polydom homolog (NvPolydom1) that shares high similarity with the Hydractinia and Hydra proteins.
source: In our study, we identified a Nematostella Polydom homolog (NvPolydom1) that shares high similarity with the Hydractinia and Hydra proteins, suggesting a conserved arrangement of domains in cnidarians (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is based on the domain analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: All Polydom and Polydom-like paralogs are expressed within the putative digestive cell state GD.1.
source: All Polydom and Polydom-like paralogs are expressed within the putative digestive cell state GD.1, with two of these showing additional expression within the uncharacterized secretory cell type S2.tll.2&3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The exceptionally high isoform diversity of Polydoms indicates a requirement for genetic robustness to account for perturbations of the developmental process regulated by the Nematostella Polydoms.
source: This, together with the exceptionally high isoform diversity, indicates a requirement for genetic robustness to account for perturbations of the developmental process regulated by the Nematostella Polydoms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed diversity of Polydom isoforms.

claim: Mouse Polydom is essential for endothelial cell migration in a Tie-dependent manner.
source: Given that mouse Polydom is essential for endothelial cell migration in a Tie-dependent manner (Sato-Nishiuchi et al., 2023), it is plausible that the Nematostella homologs could serve a similar function for rearrangement of epithelial cells along the BM during primary polyp morphogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: It is plausible that the Nematostella Polydom homologs could serve a similar function for rearrangement of epithelial cells along the basement membrane during primary polyp morphogenesis.
source: Given that mouse Polydom is essential for endothelial cell migration in a Tie-dependent manner (Sato-Nishiuchi et al., 2023), it is plausible that the Nematostella homologs could serve a similar function for rearrangement of epithelial cells along the BM during primary polyp morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the function of mouse Polydom.

claim: The top differentially abundant factor in the primary polyp mesoglea is a secreted integrin-alpha-related protein (sIntREP) containing three integrin-alpha N-terminal domains followed by a stretch of EGF repeats.
source: Interestingly, the top differentially abundant factor in the primary polyp mesoglea is a secreted integrin-alpha-related protein (sIntREP) containing three integrin-alpha N-terminal domains followed by a stretch of EGF repeats.
evidence: This is based on quantitative proteomic data.

claim: It is an attractive hypothesis that sIntREP modulates integrin-dependent cell adhesion by Polydoms and other factors to facilitate cell migration.
source: It is an attractive hypothesis that sIntREP modulates integrin-dependent cell adhesion by Polydoms and other factors to facilitate cell migration.
evidence: This is a speculation about the function of sIntREP.

claim: The enrichment of Wnt/PCP signaling components, including ROR2, protocadherin Fat4-like, and hedgling, supports the assumption of epithelial cell migration as a main driver of primary polyp morphogenesis.
source: The second group of proteins that contains several components of the Wnt/PCP pathway, including ROR2, protocadherin Fat4-like, and hedgling, further supports the assumption of epithelial cell migration as a main driver of primary polyp morphogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the proteomic data and knowledge of Wnt/PCP pathway function.

claim: Wnt/PCP signaling has a well-established role in convergent extension movements of cells during gastrulation to facilitate the elongation of the embryo along its oral-aboral axis.
source: Wnt/PCP signaling, originally described in Drosophila melanogaster (Adler, 2002; Gubb and García-Bellido, 1982), has a well-established role in convergent extension movements of cells during gastrulation to facilitate the elongation of the embryo along its oral-aboral axis (Gao, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Hydra Fat-like homolog has been reported to be polarized along the oral-aboral axis and to organize epithelial cell alignment via organization of the actin cytoskeleton.
source: Recently, the Hydra Fat-like homolog has been reported to be polarized along the oral-aboral axis and to organize epithelial cell alignment via organization of the actin cytoskeleton (Brooun et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Hedgling is an ancestral, non-bilaterian member of the cadherin superfamily with high similarity to FAT and Flamingo cadherins.
source: Hedgling is an ancestral, non-bilaterian member of the cadherin superfamily with high similarity to FAT and Flamingo cadherins (Adamska et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Hedgling has a gastrodermal expression in the Nematostella primary polyp.
source: It has a gastrodermal expression in the Nematostella primary polyp (Adamska et al., 2007), which it shares with Wnt5a and ROR2 (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and expression data.

claim: ROR2 is the principal transducer of PCP signaling via Wnt5a in the Xenopus embryo.
source: ROR2, a highly conserved receptor tyrosine kinase, is the principal transducer of PCP signaling via Wnt5a in the Xenopus embryo (Hikasa et al., 2002; Schambony and Wedlich, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: ROR2 has been reported to induce directional cell movements in mammals.
source: It has also been reported to induce directional cell movements in mammals (He et al., 2008) and to induce filopodia formation as a prerequisite for directed cell migration (Nishita et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: ROR2 induces filopodia formation as a prerequisite for directed cell migration.
source: It has also been reported to induce directional cell movements in mammals (He et al., 2008) and to induce filopodia formation as a prerequisite for directed cell migration (Nishita et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The molecular dynamics of the mesoglea suggest that massive epithelial rearrangement and directed cell migration underlie axial elongation during primary polyp morphogenesis.
source: Taken together, the molecular dynamics of the mesoglea revealed by quantitative mass spectrometry suggest that massive epithelial rearrangement and directed cell migration underlie axial elongation during primary polyp morphogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the proteomic data.

claim: Fibrillar collagens do not appear to contribute largely to the larva-to-polyp transition process.
source: Interestingly, IM components such as fibrillar collagens do not appear to contribute largely to this process.
evidence: This is based on the proteomic data showing no significant upregulation of fibrillar collagens.

claim: The adult mesoglea is significantly enriched in elastic fiber components, such as fibrillins and fibulin.
source: In contrast, the adult mesoglea is significantly enriched in elastic fiber components, such as fibrillins and fibulin.
evidence: This is based on quantitative proteomic data.

claim: The enrichment of elastic fiber components in the adult mesoglea likely adds to the visco-elastic properties of the growing body column.
source: This compositional shift likely adds to the visco-elastic properties (Gosline, 1971a; Gosline, 1971b) of the growing body column (Figure 4B and D, Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is an inference based on the proteomic data and citations about visco-elastic properties.

claim: The adult mesoglea contains several matricellular factors associated with different aspects of wound healing in vertebrate organisms.
source: In addition, the adult mesoglea contains several matricellular factors associated with different aspects of wound healing in vertebrate organisms (Cárdenas-León et al., 2022).
evidence: This is based on proteomic data and a citation.

claim: The Nematostella uromodulin gene was previously reported to be highly upregulated in the wound ectoderm, likely contributing to the innate immune response.
source: The Nematostella uromodulin gene was previously reported to be highly upregulated in the wound ectoderm, likely contributing to the innate immune response (DuBuc et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: While metalloproteases are similarly upregulated in adults and primary polyps, there is a noticeable increase of diverse classes of protease inhibitors in adults (7 vs 2 in primary polyps).
source: Indeed, while metalloproteases are similarly upregulated in adults and primary polyps, we observed a noticeable increase of diverse classes of protease inhibitors in adults (7 vs 2 in primary polyps), including TIMP, Kunitz and Kazal-type protease inhibitors, as well as thyroglobulin repeat proteins (Novinec et al., 2006; Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This is based on quantitative proteomic data.

claim: The increase of protease inhibitors in adults is indicative of a high degree of protease activity regulation in tissue morphogenesis during growth.
source: This is indicative of a high degree of protease activity regulation in tissue morphogenesis during growth, as also observed during Nematostella whole-body regeneration (Schaffer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on the proteomic data and a citation.

claim: The transition from the primary polyp to the adult is characterized by an increase of elastic fibrillar IM components contributing to the long-range elasticity and resilience of the mesoglea, and a recruitment of wound response factors.
source: Taken together, the transition from the primary polyp to the adult is characterized by an increase of elastic fibrillar IM components contributing to the long-range elasticity and resilience of the mesoglea, and a recruitment of wound response factors that together with a complex network of proteases and protease inhibitors likely regulate growth, organogenesis, and tissue differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the proteomic data.

claim: Wound response factors together with a complex network of proteases and protease inhibitors likely regulate growth, organogenesis, and tissue differentiation in adult polyps.
source: Taken together, the transition from the primary polyp to the adult is characterized by an increase of elastic fibrillar IM components contributing to the long-range elasticity and resilience of the mesoglea, and a recruitment of wound response factors that together with a complex network of proteases and protease inhibitors likely regulate growth, organogenesis, and tissue differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the proteomic data.

claim: The evolution of the ECM is closely linked to the emergence of metazoan life forms.
source: The evolution of extracellular matrix, a complex network of secreted, typically modular proteins, is closely linked to the emergence of metazoan life forms (Hynes, 2009; Hynes, 2012; Naba, 2024; Ozbek et al., 2010; Rokas, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ctenophores have recently been identified as the sister group to all other animals.
source: Although ctenophores have recently been identified as the sister group to all other animals (Schultz et al., 2023), the hitherto available genomic evidence suggests that they possess only a minimal repertoire of conserved ECM and ECM-affiliated proteins, limiting comparative studies with bilaterians (Draper et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Ctenophores possess only a minimal repertoire of conserved ECM and ECM-affiliated proteins, limiting comparative studies with bilaterians.
source: Although ctenophores have recently been identified as the sister group to all other animals (Schultz et al., 2023), the hitherto available genomic evidence suggests that they possess only a minimal repertoire of conserved ECM and ECM-affiliated proteins, limiting comparative studies with bilaterians (Draper et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Cnidarian genome data have offered broad evidence for conserved matrisomes anticipating the complexity of mammalian species.
source: In contrast, cnidarian genome data have offered broad evidence for conserved matrisomes anticipating the complexity of mammalian species (Tucker and Adams, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The study analyzed the dynamics of 287 ECM factors by TMT labeling and LC-MS/MS of decellularized mesoglea samples from different life stages.
source: Here, we identified 551 ECM proteins that comprise the matrisome of the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis through in silico prediction using transcriptome databases and analyzed the dynamics of 287 ECM factors by TMT labeling and LC-MS/MS of decellularized mesoglea samples from different life stages.
evidence: This describes the methodology of the study.

claim: The finding that the inner gastroderm is the major source of the Nematostella ECM supports the model of germ layer evolution where the cnidarian inner cell layer (endoderm) is homologous to the bilaterian mesoderm.
source: Utilizing cell-type-specific atlases, we showed that the inner gastroderm is the major source of the Nematostella ECM, including all 12 collagen-encoding genes. This finding supports the model of germ layer evolution proposed by Steinmetz et al., 2017 where, based on both transcription factor profiles and structural gene sets, the cnidarian inner cell layer (endoderm) is homologous to the bilaterian mesoderm that gives rise to connective tissues.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression data and supported by a citation.

claim: The finding that the gastrodermis is the major source of ECM contrasts the situation in Hydra where both germ layers contribute to the synthesis of core matrisome proteins.
source: It also contrasts the situation in Hydra where both germ layers contribute to the synthesis of core matrisome proteins (Epp et al., 1986; Zhang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a comparison with Hydra supported by citations.

claim: The primacy of the gastrodermis in ECM synthesis might be related to the anthozoan-specific mesenteries.
source: The primacy of the gastrodermis in ECM synthesis might be related to the anthozoan-specific mesenteries, which represent extensions of the mesoglea into the body cavity sandwiched by two endodermal layers.
evidence: This is a speculation about the reason for gastrodermal ECM synthesis.

claim: Discrete endo- and ectodermal ECM transcript repertoires would result in a restricted composition of the mesoglea in mesenteric folds.
source: The primacy of the gastrodermis in ECM synthesis might be related to the anthozoan-specific mesenteries, which represent extensions of the mesoglea into the body cavity sandwiched by two endodermal layers. Discrete endo- and ectodermal ECM transcript repertoires would result in a restricted composition of the mesoglea in these mesenteric folds.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the previous statement about mesenteries.

claim: Anthozoans have previously been considered a basal group among cnidarians.
source: While anthozoans such as Nematostella have previously been considered a basal group among cnidarians (Bridge et al., 1992; Miller et al., 2000), more recent phylogenomic studies consider them as a sister clade to medusozoans (DeBiasse et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: More recent phylogenomic studies consider anthozoans as a sister clade to medusozoans.
source: While anthozoans such as Nematostella have previously been considered a basal group among cnidarians (Bridge et al., 1992; Miller et al., 2000), more recent phylogenomic studies consider them as a sister clade to medusozoans (DeBiasse et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Anthozoan species generally exhibit a higher matrisome complexity than medusozoans.
source: Interestingly, anthozoan species generally exhibit a higher complexity than medusozoans and populate a transitory region between bilaterians and non-bilaterians in the evolutionary trajectory.
evidence: This is based on the comparison of matrisome sizes shown in Figure 5.

claim: Anthozoan species populate a transitory region between bilaterians and non-bilaterians in the evolutionary trajectory of matrisome complexity.
source: Interestingly, anthozoan species generally exhibit a higher complexity than medusozoans and populate a transitory region between bilaterians and non-bilaterians in the evolutionary trajectory.
evidence: This is based on the comparison of matrisome sizes shown in Figure 5.

claim: The acquisition of complex life cycles in medusozoa was not accompanied by a diversification of the matrisome repertoire.
source: This indicates that the acquisition of complex life cycles in medusozoa, that are distinguished by the pelagic medusa stage, was not accompanied by a diversification of the matrisome repertoire.
evidence: This is an inference based on the matrisome size comparison.

claim: Findings from genome data in Aurelia questioned the hypothesis of the medusozoan body plan being derived.
source: This is in line with findings from genome data in Aurelia, a cnidarian with a medusa stage, that questioned the hypothesis of the medusozoan body plan being derived. Rather, the authors found a redeployment of the existing genetic repertoire (Gold et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The reduced complexity of the medusozoan ECM might represent a strategy to minimize the cost for ECM remodeling during metamorphosis.
source: The reduced complexity of the medusozoan ECM might therefore represent a strategy to minimize the cost for ECM remodeling during metamorphosis and rely on a restricted set of conserved genes to form the expanded jellyfish mesoglea.
evidence: This is a speculation about the reason for reduced medusozoan ECM complexity.

claim: A significant fraction of Nematostella's exceptionally rich matrisome is devoted to the formation of the cnidocyst.
source: A significant fraction of Nematostella's exceptionally rich matrisome is devoted to the formation of the cnidocyst, a unique cellular novelty of the cnidarian clade (Babonis et al., 2023; Jékely et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on the analysis of cnidocyte-expressed genes and supported by citations.

claim: Cnidocyst-specific proteins follow an unusual secretion route into the lumen of the growing cnidocyst vesicle, which topologically represents extracellular space.
source: Cnidocyst-specific proteins follow an unusual secretion route into the lumen of the growing cnidocyst vesicle, which topologically represents extracellular space (Ozbek, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: It has been speculated that cnidocyst-specific proteins originated from neurosecretory vesicles used for predation in early metazoans.
source: It has therefore been speculated that they originated from neurosecretory vesicles used for predation in early metazoans (Balasubramanian et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by a citation.

claim: The finding that cnidocysts are instrumental for the predatory lifestyle of the Aiptasia larvae supports the hypothesis of a deeply rooted extrusive mechanism for prey capture in metazoan evolution.
source: The recent finding that cnidocysts are instrumental for the predatory lifestyle of the Aiptasia larvae (Maegele et al., 2023) supports the hypothesis of a deeply rooted extrusive mechanism for prey capture in metazoan evolution.
evidence: This is an inference based on a cited finding.

claim: The majority of Nematostella cnidocyte genes shared with other cell types is expressed within neuroglandular subtypes.
source: In this context, it is intriguing that the majority of Nematostella cnidocyte genes shared with other cell types is expressed within neuroglandular subtypes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on single-cell RNA expression data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The cnidocyst-specific matrisome contains diverse proteins with repetitive ECM domains that likely have general bioadhesive or fibrous properties that might play a role in entangling and ingesting prey organisms.
source: In addition, the cnidocyst-specific matrisome contains diverse proteins with repetitive ECM domains that likely have general bioadhesive or fibrous properties that might play a role in entangling and ingesting prey organisms.
evidence: This is a speculation about the function of these proteins.

claim: The changes in the matrisome profiles across Nematostella's major life stages suggest a highly dynamic epithelial rearrangement during primary polyp morphogenesis.
source: The changes in the matrisome profiles across Nematostella's major life stages suggest a highly dynamic epithelial rearrangement during primary polyp morphogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the proteomic data.

claim: The involvement of Wnt/PCP factors in larva-to-polyp transition indicates similar cell migration and reorientation events as during convergent extension processes in gastrulation.
source: The involvement of Wnt/PCP factors in this process indicates similar cell migration and reorientation events as during convergent extension processes in gastrulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the proteomic data and knowledge of Wnt/PCP function.

claim: Primary archenteron invagination and apical constriction of bottle cells in Nematostella is dependent on the PCP components strabismus and Fzd10.
source: Kumburegama et al. have shown that primary archenteron invagination and apical constriction of bottle cells in Nematostella is dependent on the PCP components strabismus (Kumburegama et al., 2011) and Fzd10 (Wijesena et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Mesentery formation in primary polyps likely involves similar molecular pathways as archenteron invagination.
source: Mesentery formation in primary polyps, which involves sequential folding events of the endodermal epithelium (Berking, 2007), likely involves similar molecular pathways.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the similarity of the processes and a citation.

claim: Mesoglea synthesis follows invagination during mesentery formation.
source: As already observed by Appelöf, 1900, mesoglea synthesis follows invagination during this process.
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The molecular network composed of Wnt/PCP and basal membrane factors might indicate an actomyosin-controlled invagination of the endodermal layer followed by basement membrane production to re-align the cells in their apico-basal architecture.
source: The molecular network composed of Wnt/PCP and basal membrane factors that our data revealed might therefore indicate an actomyosin-controlled invagination of the endodermal layer followed by BM production to re-align the cells in their apico-basal architecture.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the proteomic data.

claim: The upregulation of wound response factors in the adult animal might indicate a transient loss of tissue integrity during collective cell migration.
source: The upregulation of wound response factors in the adult animal might indicate a transient loss of tissue integrity during collective cell migration, which could entail an actin-based purse-string mechanism as during wound healing (Begnaud et al., 2016; Bischoff et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the proteomic data and supported by citations.
